correctness.rationale: The exact absolute-sine Fourier expansion gives a nonnegative sum of squared Fourier magnitudes for the generator-count-normalized deficit. Angular orthogonality and two exact spectral sums yield the displayed first moment and the finite-sample variance in RESULT.md. A multivariate central limit theorem, nonnegative uniform Fourier-tail control and the Euler sine product give the radial-second-moment-scaled exponential-series limit and its transform. Including the centered length yields an independent normal limit because all cross covariances vanish. In the triangular array, the exact area identity and the independently derived finite-sample area variance establish the sharp crossover and limiting variance. The standalone checker replays geometric area, Fourier identities, moments, and critical-scale samples; simulations are not used to prove infinite limits.

originality.rationale: The evaluated fixed-length isotropic spectral distribution and transform are explicitly prior work (opaque finding 474c5a5f-f684-4deb-8225-2bcddca2d7a3), not the new content. The claimed original unit is the universal positive independent radial-length extension, exact finite radial variance/covariance, asymptotic decoupling of radial and angular geometry, and sharp triangular-array Gaussian/non-Gaussian crossover. Schneider 2202.06774 establishes expected valuations and a first-order nondegenerate U-statistic CLT rather than this second-order perimeter-cancelled joint law; other inspected sources concern deterministic zonotope inequalities, lattice-generator models or fixed-azimuth approximations. Priority is provisional and unindexed stronger coverage remains a specific residual risk.

value.rationale: This is a motivated analysis of shape-versus-size geometry statistics for i.i.d. isotropic zonogons: exact finite-sample second moments for arbitrary radial distributions, a universal second-order isoperimetric deficit law scaled by the radial second moment, joint asymptotic decoupling from perimeter fluctuations, and a sharp radial standard-deviation threshold at \(n^{-1/2}\) producing an explicit continuum of Gaussian convolutions of a known non-Gaussian distribution. The result predicts stochastic geometry in a regime where the fluctuation scaling changes, describes an exact finite-sample variance, and goes beyond a renamed unit-length case. The prior unit-length transform is expressly credited.
